verdict.rationale: Ubuntu documents installing on hardware you choose: replacing Windows or dual-booting, extending the life of older machines, certified Raspberry Pi (Arm) support, availability across Dell, HP and Lenovo, and guides for NVIDIA drivers and Intel RST/BitLocker during installation. However, the evidence never explicitly addresses freedom from vendor lock-in, and hardware breadth is only vendor-claimed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of no vendor lock-in (open licensing, no proprietary tie-in), a documented hardware compatibility scope beyond named OEMs and the Pi, independent or hands-on corroboration of broad hardware support.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can install and use the OS without vendor lock-in on hardware of my choosing
